chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Crawford's Grill drummer Honey Boy; how Roy started on trumpet
summary: In Pittsburgh he stayed to watch a fire-throwing drummer, and says Roy began as a drummer until his brother Joe bought him a trumpet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: No, not any more. I got another guitar from home, and I stayed in Pittsburgh because I wanted to stay with the man. It wasn't easy, you know, but I used to go to a club called Crawford's Grill and they had a very good band there, and they had a drummer there that fascinated me. They called him Honey Boy. Honey Boy would play these drums, he was a wizard, and he had emery wheels on the end of his sticks, and somehow he worked these emery wheels and the fire would come out of the sticks, you know. And I would go -- but there was -- despite that it was a very good band, and Roy would come and jam every night. Because Roy's a frustrated drummer also. You know, I think Roy's first instrument was a drum. But his brother, who plays saxophone, Joe Eldridge, had to always help him with his drums. So Joe bought him a trumpet, and told him to say, hey, kid, learn this. I'm tired of carrying these damned drums. So this is how Roy started playing trumpet.
